Definition: Barakel, the father of one of Job's friends
BiblicalUsage: Barakel is named only as the father of Elihu the Buzite, the young man who speaks last in the book of Job. He speaks after the three friends fall silent.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that a father's name is kept here so we know Elihu is a real man with a family, not a voice out of nowhere, and his words carry weight because he waited his turn to speak.
